newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal opposition lodges no-confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: Nepal opposition lodges no-confidence motion.

text.p: Nepal's communist opposition on Wednesday formally lodged a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's 15-month-old government.
The United Marxist-Leninist (UML) party said it registered the notice with parliament, which by an earlier order of King Birendra had been summoned to begin debating the motion next Monday.
Under the Himalayan kingdom's five-year-old constitution, a vote on the motion cannot be held until at least 10 days after the date it is registered.

The communists, who had earlier signalled they would lodge the no-confidence motion, were bolstered by a breakaway faction of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), one of three partners in the tenuous governing coalition.
On Sunday, 11 rebel RPP deputies announced they were withdrawing support for Deuba's coalition, which had controlled 108 seats in the 205-seat lower house.
Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party has 86 lawmakers. The RPP, considered close to the monarchy, has 19 seats and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP) has three.
To topple Deuba, his opponents would need at least 103 votes. Nepal's constitution requires the motion be passed by a majority of the 205-member house.
Deuba said on Tuesday that his opponents would fail to muster 103 votes from among the 200 sitting members.
United Marxist-Leninist party general secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal told Reuters on Wednesday that 102 deputies had so far backed the motion.
The UML, with 87 deputies, and 11 RPP rebels have the support of two independents and say they also command support from two NSP members. The NSP has disputed the claim.
Three deputies from the leftist Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party, which has a tradition of voting independently, could settle Deuba's fate, political analysts say.
Seven of the RPP rebels were ministers who resigned from Deuba's cabinet this week. The RPP rebels accused Deuba of harassing RPP's political activists.

King Birendra on Wednesday accepted the resignation of Local Development Minister Kamal Thapa, one of the seven rebels, officials said. Deuba was still in talks with the six other RPP ministers, politicians said.
The communists formed a minority government after general elections in November 1994 produced a hung parliament. They were toppled last year when the three main opposition parties joined ranks.
